nodes.label: Committed program identity
nodes.rationale: A valid proof of substituted code must not satisfy the authorized claim.

nodes.label: Effect constraints
nodes.rationale: Recipient, asset, debit, receipt, fee, writes and approvals are explicit semantic constraints.

nodes.label: Authenticated evidence sidecar
nodes.rationale: Content addressing can separate evidence storage while preserving mandatory semantic authorization.

nodes.label: Adversarial binding mutation suite
nodes.rationale: Mutate transaction, chain, code, verifier, specification, state, effects, expiry, evidence and claim root; passing is test coverage rather than absence-of-bugs proof.

nodes.label: Proof-system soundness
nodes.rationale: Soundness establishes existence of a witness for a particular relation under its cryptographic assumptions.

nodes.label: Signed mandatory-claim root
nodes.rationale: Authorization over semantic claims prevents relays from stripping mandatory conditions.

nodes.label: Signed intent
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable constraints must match what the human authorized; wallet rendering remains a trust boundary.

nodes.label: Semantic acceptance theorem
nodes.rationale: Combines sound evidence, bindings, adequate specification, current applicability and external assumptions.

nodes.label: SP1 proof stack
nodes.rationale: Report uses disclosed recursive constraint/binding failures to motivate explicit proof-stack trust boundaries.

nodes.label: Adequate committed specification
nodes.rationale: Proof soundness is useful only if the committed relation expresses the intended requirement.

nodes.label: Statement binding
nodes.rationale: Evidence must bind the exact domain, transaction, intent, code, specification, verifier, state and effects.

nodes.label: Proof-independent transaction core
nodes.rationale: Two-stage commitments avoid circular dependence between transaction identity and embedded evidence.

nodes.label: Human-to-policy intent capture
nodes.rationale: A compromised wallet may show one policy and sign another; evidence cannot repair that mismatch.

nodes.label: Valid execution with wrong recipient
nodes.rationale: A correctly executed swap can send proceeds to Mallory; execution soundness alone does not satisfy Alice signed intent.

nodes.label: Proof-Carrying Transactions report
nodes.rationale: User-supplied secondary research report with opaque citation markers; its explicit assertions are not independently verified facts.

nodes.label: Proof-carrying transaction
nodes.rationale: Layered design pattern; attaching evidence does not by itself establish recursively compliant history.

nodes.label: Proof-Carrying Transaction Claim Envelope
nodes.rationale: Typed authenticated claims separate intended properties from evidence-system selection.

nodes.label: Semantic safety prototype
nodes.rationale: Canonical envelope, narrow intent language and an independent effect checker are judged by rejecting ledger-valid intent violations.

nodes.label: Cardano extended UTxO
nodes.rationale: Explicit consumed and reference inputs support dependency binding; canonical presence remains a ledger check.

nodes.label: History compliance predicate
nodes.rationale: The recursive relation must connect predecessor statements and admissible transformations.

nodes.label: Consensus finality
nodes.rationale: Cross-chain event membership requires an authenticated accepted source history.

nodes.label: Global uniqueness and ordering
nodes.rationale: Local note or transition validity cannot independently prevent global double spending.

nodes.label: Halo2 proof technology
nodes.rationale: Availability of recursion in a proof technology is distinct from whether a particular application or source language uses it.

nodes.label: Zcash Orchard bundle proofs
nodes.rationale: Report explicitly describes Orchard usage as nonrecursive; this is a property of the Orchard design, not all Halo2 uses.

nodes.label: Proof-carrying data
nodes.rationale: Current data and predecessor histories satisfy a prescribed compliance predicate.

nodes.label: Simulation-extractable PCD
nodes.rationale: Standalone security notions do not automatically establish adversarial recursive composition security.

nodes.label: Authenticated input-state reference
nodes.rationale: Proof statements identify the state against which the computation was justified.

nodes.label: Cross-party witness handoff
nodes.rationale: Extending a proof must be assessed for custody, privacy and availability dependencies caused by private accumulator transfer.

nodes.label: Holography accumulation
nodes.rationale: Report describes a 2026 stateless-recursive-proving research construction, not production readiness.

nodes.label: Multi-folding PCD
nodes.rationale: Targets distributed DAG computation; author-reported benchmarks are not universal transaction costs.

nodes.label: Shielded client-side validation
nodes.rationale: Direct research example of recipient history validation with chain-anchored uniqueness, not an established deployment.

nodes.label: Multi-party provenance prototype
nodes.rationale: Branch and join across parties while keeping each participant private witness material private.

nodes.label: Semantic property composition
nodes.rationale: Verifying child proofs requires state-root compatibility and a rule for combining policies.

nodes.label: Data and witness availability
nodes.rationale: Validity and compression do not ensure that participants can obtain data required to continue.

nodes.label: End-to-end proof economics
nodes.rationale: Compare witness acquisition, proving, aggregation, stale retries and replicated verification against replicated execution.

nodes.label: Independent verifier implementations
nodes.rationale: The report proposes differential agreement and stable vectors before mandatory consensus deployment.

nodes.label: Application invariant claim
nodes.rationale: Preservation is relative to stated preconditions, specification and environmental assumptions.

nodes.label: Ordinary ledger acceptance
nodes.rationale: Consensus validity and deterministic state transition remain distinct components of the full semantic acceptance condition.

nodes.label: Network-wide inductive invariant
nodes.rationale: Base-state validity and preservation by every permitted transition are required, including upgrades and emergency paths.

nodes.label: State-churn reproof cost
nodes.rationale: Relevant state mutations during proof generation can dominate end-to-end cost and latency.

nodes.label: Verifier upgrade and revocation
nodes.rationale: Version migration and revocation require exercised safety behavior before stronger deployment claims.

nodes.label: EIP-8025 optional execution proofs
nodes.rationale: Report describes a proposal allowing optional validation acceleration without changing validity rules.

nodes.label: Execution accelerator prototype
nodes.rationale: Compare a proof path to conventional execution under identical validity semantics and measured total costs.

nodes.label: Optional execution acceleration
nodes.rationale: Conventional execution may replace optional acceleration only while preserving the same validity rules.

nodes.label: Authenticated-fragment proof
nodes.rationale: Checks individual dependencies instead of invalidating solely because an unrelated global state root changed.

nodes.label: Conditional transition proof
nodes.rationale: Proves an effect for every current state satisfying a stated precondition.

nodes.label: Authenticated dependency footprint
nodes.rationale: Membership of declared accesses is weaker than completeness of the read/write set.

nodes.label: Reusable formal certificate
nodes.rationale: A trusted kernel checks a committed precondition/program/postcondition certificate.

nodes.label: Current-state applicability
nodes.rationale: Historical proof validity does not establish that dependencies remain applicable at inclusion.

nodes.label: Guard and path conditions
nodes.rationale: Certificate reuse depends on entry function, guard and path hash, not arbitrary contract execution.

nodes.label: Theorem-Carrying Transactions
nodes.rationale: Reusable guarded-path semantic certificate prototype; the report does not establish production theorem consensus.

nodes.label: Compiler and circuit correspondence
nodes.rationale: Underconstrained generated relations can diverge from source semantics despite valid proof verification.

nodes.label: Conditional receipt assumptions
nodes.rationale: Assumptions introduced by inner verification must be discharged for an unconditional outer receipt.

nodes.label: Execution correctness
nodes.rationale: Correct committed-machine execution does not establish intended purpose or current applicability.

nodes.label: Execution-specific property
nodes.rationale: A property of one execution or guarded path is weaker than an all-executions theorem.

nodes.label: Mina proof-authorized updates and chain recursion
nodes.norm_label: mina proof-authorized updates and chain recursion
nodes.rationale: Adjacent architecture; authorization does not imply all application properties.

nodes.label: Program-wide property
nodes.rationale: Requires explicit quantification over the stated domain and appropriate formal evidence.

nodes.label: RISC Zero receipts
nodes.rationale: General execution evidence and recursive assumption resolution; guest program correctness is separate.

nodes.label: Canonical encoding and domain separation
nodes.rationale: Consistent decoding and hashing prevent interpretation and substitution disagreements.

nodes.label: Claim dependency graph
nodes.rationale: Explicit dependencies are part of the envelope and require semantic consistency checks.

nodes.label: Mandatory safety claim
nodes.rationale: Unknown mandatory claims cause rejection; mandatory evidence must not silently fall back to an unchecked path.

nodes.label: Validity interval
nodes.rationale: The claim has explicit start and end conditions checked against the inclusion environment.

nodes.label: Verification cost budget
nodes.rationale: Cheap prerequisite checks and explicit verification budgets bound invalid-proof admission work.

nodes.label: Verifier authority and version
nodes.rationale: The relying party chooses permitted predicates and verifiers; the prover cannot choose an arbitrary approving verifier.

nodes.label: Compact bounded source language
nodes.rationale: Report says direct source-language recursion is disallowed; backend recursive proof composition is a separate capability question.

nodes.label: External-world truth assumptions
nodes.rationale: Authenticated oracle and credential assertions do not prove real-world truth, solvency or legal compliance.

nodes.label: Midnight proof-bearing transactions
nodes.rationale: Report describes private computation, transcript, verifier key and current-state checks. Its Compact recursion restriction does not establish absence of Midnight backend recursion.

nodes.label: Private authorization and eligibility
nodes.rationale: Proof authenticates possession and encoded policy satisfaction without manufacturing issuer truth.

nodes.label: Abstract resource bounds
nodes.rationale: Finite steps, memory, calls and state bytes do not themselves imply a wall-clock latency guarantee.

nodes.label: PCD from accumulation
nodes.rationale: Accumulation can build PCD under the cited construction assumptions.

nodes.label: Incrementally verifiable computation
nodes.rationale: Sequential certified steps are an important building block, not automatically cross-party DAG PCD.

nodes.label: Neo and SuperNeo
nodes.rationale: Report describes small-field and post-quantum-oriented folding research; end-to-end production claims are not established.

nodes.label: Nova folding
nodes.rationale: Reported sequential IVC construction; operational suitability for mutually distrustful producers is a separate question.
